column1: # Where each woven Latin present participle in lex-la.tsv was read.
# A verb row weaves its second form under an English -ing, and the tooltip
# prints that form as the word the reader met. Its sound has been held to
# Allen & Greenough since 2026-10-04, and its spelling to nothing: Lewis &
# Short prints a verb's principal parts, not its participle. English
# Wiktionary conjugates every Latin verb in a table whose cells carry a class
# per slot, and on 2026-10-08 every woven participle was read in the rendered
# table (action=render) of its entry: the cell classed pres|act|part, quoted
# as the table prints it, "present active participle movēns".
# tests/tools/la-forms.test.ts fails on a form changed in one file and not
# the other, a line citing another verb's entry, a quote from another cell or
# not printing its form, and a line outliving its row.
# One entry per line, the one whose table the quote is from:
# A noun's is its headword's. Wiktionary files a verb under its first
# person, the key Lewis & Short files it under in la-glosses.tsv, so a verb's
# is that key's, j written i and the homograph number dropped: dīcere is
# A page holding more than one word of a spelling is read by the table whose
# headword is this one, Wiktionary marking each table's with its vowel
# lengths: ōs, the mouth, "ōra", beside os, the bone, "ossa, ossua"; liber,
# 78 of the 79 are among the forms their table prints. nārrāre, "tell", is
# woven nārrāns, where the table prints "narrāns": Wiktionary marks the
# first vowel short, the seed long, which is a question about the headword's
# own length, not the participle's, and QUEUED in tests/tools/la-forms.test.ts
# names it until a dictionary is read for it.
